paper_quote: The research in this paper uses actual earnings announcement dates (as reported by Standard and Poor’s) in an attempt to avoid this problem.

The research in this paper uses cut-off points based on a ranking of the previous quarter's earnings forecast errors to assign firms into one of ten forecast error portfolios, and all observations in a given portfolio are weighted equally.
Firms that were publicly listed in 1973 but were delisted prior to 1982 are excluded from the 1982 tape.
The 1982 Compustat tape, covering 2,454 companies, was the initial data base examined.

The first screen, requiring each company to have at least ten consecutive earnings observations, reduced the sample to 2,213 companies.

Early versions of the quarterly Compustat tape were then used to build for each company (if available) a quarterly earnings file covering the second quarter of 1970 to the fourth quarter of the 1981 period.
The cumulative abnormal return (CAR) results reported in this paper cover the 1974 to 1981 period.
The pre-1974 period is used in estimating univariate time-series models.
The minimum number of observations in any one quarter is 1,495 while the maximum number is 1,978.

\text{FE}_i^1 = \frac{Q_{i,t} - E(Q_{i,t})}{|Q_{i,t}|} \quad (9)
\text{FE}_i^2 = \frac{Q_{i,t} - E(Q_{i,t})}{\sigma[Q_{i,t} - E(Q_{i,t})]} \quad (10)
\text{FE}_i^3 = \frac{\sum_{t=-1}^{0} \tilde{u}_{i,t}}{\sigma(\tilde{u}_{i,t})} \quad (12)
\sigma(\tilde{u}_{i,t}) = \text{the standard deviation of } \tilde{u}_{i,t} \text{ in the 250-trading-day period prior to the } [-1, 0] \text{ event time period being examined.}
\text{FE}_i^4 = \frac{\left( \sum_{t=-60}^{0} \tilde{u}_{i,t} \right) / 61}{\sigma(\tilde{u}_{i,t})} \quad (13)
\sum_{t=-60}^{0} \tilde{u}_{i,t} = \text{the cumulative abnormal return in the 61-trading-day period up to and including the day of the earnings announcement, and}
\sigma(\tilde{u}_{i,t}) = \text{the standard deviation of } \tilde{u}_{i,t} \text{ in the 250-trading-day period prior to the } [-60, 0] \text{ event time period being examined.}
